lines.text: Lesson twenty: evaluating an entry opportunity. A careful checklist that can end in no trade.
lines.say: Lesson twenty: evaluating an entry opportunity. A careful checklist that can end in no trade.

lines.text: Here's a fictional BTC chart. The last few candles are green, and price is near 60,000.
lines.say: Here's a fictional B-T-C chart. The last few candles are green, and price is near sixty thousand.

lines.text: It's tempting to press BUY right now. But what do we actually know?
lines.say: It's tempting to press buy right now. But what do we actually know?

lines.text: Instead of guessing, let's check the chart step by step.
lines.say: Instead of guessing, let's check the chart step by step.

lines.text: An entry opportunity is a moment when you consider opening a trade. Considering is not entering.
lines.say: An entry opportunity is a moment when you consider opening a trade. Considering is not entering.

lines.text: Like a pilot before take-off: the same checks, in the same order, every time.
lines.say: Like a pilot before take-off: the same checks, in the same order, every time.

lines.text: Trend, range, zones, volume, risk. Only then a tentative decision: buy, sell or wait.
lines.say: Trend, range, zones, volume, risk. Only then a tentative decision: buy, sell or wait.

lines.text: Step one: the trend. A trend is the general direction price has been moving.
lines.say: Step one: the trend. A trend is the general direction price has been moving.

lines.text: Over this hour, the lows kept getting higher. That leans up.
lines.say: Over this hour, the lows kept getting higher. That leans up.

lines.text: But the last high was lower than the one before. So: up, but choppy. Not a clear signal.
lines.say: But the last high was lower than the one before. So: up, but choppy. Not a clear signal.

lines.text: Step two: the recent range. The space between the recent high and the recent low.
lines.say: Step two: the recent range. The space between the recent high and the recent low.

lines.text: Over the last eight candles: high 60,100, low 59,500. That's 600 USDT.
lines.say: Over the last eight candles: high sixty thousand one hundred, low fifty-nine thousand five hundred. That's six hundred U-S-D-T.

lines.text: 600 out of 60,000 is about 1%. And price now sits near the top of this box.
lines.say: Six hundred out of sixty thousand is about one percent. And price now sits near the top of this box.

lines.text: Step three: zones. Support is like a floor where falls often paused. Resistance is like a ceiling.
lines.say: Step three: zones. Support is like a floor where falls often paused. Resistance is like a ceiling.

lines.text: Here, resistance sits at 60,050 to 60,150. Support sits at 59,500 to 59,600.
lines.say: Here, resistance sits at sixty thousand fifty to sixty thousand one hundred fifty. Support sits at fifty-nine thousand five hundred to fifty-nine thousand six hundred.

lines.text: Price is at 60,000, just under resistance. Only about 50 USDT of room before the ceiling.
lines.say: Price is at sixty thousand, just under resistance. Only about fifty U-S-D-T of room before the ceiling.

lines.text: Step four: volume is how much was traded in each candle. Liquidity is how easily you can trade.
lines.say: Step four: volume is how much was traded in each candle. Liquidity is how easily you can trade.

lines.text: The big drop and first push up had high volume. This last push up has less and less.
lines.say: The big drop and first push up had high volume. This last push up has less and less.

lines.text: Fading volume is a weak sign, not proof. Volume alone never tells you the direction.
lines.say: Fading volume is a weak sign, not proof. Volume alone never tells you the direction.

lines.text: Step five: your risk budget. The most you accept to lose on this one trade, decided before entering.
lines.say: Step five: your risk budget. The most you accept to lose on this one trade, decided before entering.

lines.text: Example only: a 1,000 USDT practice account, and a risk budget of 10 USDT.
lines.say: Example only: a one thousand U-S-D-T practice account, and a risk budget of ten U-S-D-T.

lines.text: A stop below support at 59,400 is 600 USDT away: 1%. Sized for that, a loss is about 10 USDT.
lines.say: A stop below support at fifty-nine thousand four hundred is six hundred U-S-D-T away: one percent. Sized for that, a loss is about ten U-S-D-T.

lines.text: If price reaches 60,100, the gain is only about 1.7 USDT, and fees take about 1 of it.
lines.say: If price reaches sixty thousand one hundred, the gain is only about one point seven U-S-D-T, and fees take about one of it.

lines.text: Step six: a tentative decision. Buy, sell or wait, and you write down why.
lines.say: Step six: a tentative decision. Buy, sell or wait, and you write down why.

lines.text: Mild uptrend, but price is under resistance, volume is fading, and the reward is tiny next to the risk.
lines.say: Mild uptrend, but price is under resistance, volume is fading, and the reward is tiny next to the risk.

lines.text: So the decision is WAIT. No trade is a real, sensible result of the checklist.
lines.say: So the decision is wait. No trade is a real, sensible result of the checklist.

lines.text: A common mistake: deciding the direction first, then looking for reasons to agree.
lines.say: A common mistake: deciding the direction first, then looking for reasons to agree.

lines.text: Green candles alone are not a reason. Work through the checklist in order, and write your why.
lines.say: Green candles alone are not a reason. Work through the checklist in order, and write your why.

lines.text: And WAIT is not a failure. It's often the best answer when the signals don't line up.
lines.say: And wait is not a failure. It's often the best answer when the signals don't line up.

lines.text: Your turn. A different fictional coin, checklist filled in. What's the sensible tentative decision?
lines.say: Your turn. A different fictional coin, checklist filled in. What's the sensible tentative decision?

lines.text: Pause if you need more time. Is it A, B or C?
lines.say: Pause if you need more time. Is it A, B or C?

lines.text: C, wait. Every signal is neutral, so there's no reason to take the risk.
lines.say: C, wait. Every signal is neutral, so there's no reason to take the risk.

lines.text: A is tempting, but one green candle is not a reason. Neutral signals mean no trade.
lines.say: A is tempting, but one green candle is not a reason. Neutral signals mean no trade.

lines.text: Before using any checklist, know its limits.
lines.say: Before using any checklist, know its limits.

lines.text: A checklist cannot predict the future. Price can still move against you.
lines.say: A checklist cannot predict the future. Price can still move against you.

lines.text: Stops can slip, and fees eat small gains. Leverage makes losses bigger.
lines.say: Stops can slip, and fees eat small gains. Leverage makes losses bigger.

lines.text: These are fictional examples, not advice. When signals are unclear, WAIT is always allowed.
lines.say: These are fictional examples, not advice. When signals are unclear, wait is always allowed.

lines.text: Let's recap.
lines.say: Let's recap.

lines.text: One: check in order. Trend, range, zones, volume, then your risk budget.
lines.say: One: check in order. Trend, range, zones, volume, then your risk budget.

lines.text: Two: a decision needs reasons. Write down why, not only the direction.
lines.say: Two: a decision needs reasons. Write down why, not only the direction.

lines.text: Three: when signals are neutral or mixed, WAIT is a real decision.
lines.say: Three: when signals are neutral or mixed, wait is a real decision.

lines.text: Check yourself: price is just under resistance and volume is fading. A strong buy?
lines.say: Check yourself: price is just under resistance and volume is fading. A strong buy?

lines.text: No. Those are reasons to wait.
lines.say: No. Those are reasons to wait.

lines.text: Next up: T21, confirmation, false signals and NO_TRADE. Why waiting is a decision too.
lines.say: Next up: T twenty-one, confirmation, false signals and no trade. Why waiting is a decision too.
